## Reflection

The high-dose acquisitions drove the correct call: tub_glcm_contrast z=+121.7 and tub_std z=+69.7 at 3 uM with replication at 1 uM, plus microscopist-reported bundling and 5/10 atlas matches to microtubule stabilizers, all separated stabilizers from destabilizers that would lower tub_mean.

The potentially misleading signals were minor: 2/10 atlas hits to Protein degradation kept a 0.05 alternative early, and the tub_mean rho=+0.80 and cell_count rho=-0.80 dose trends were non-significant with p=0.2 from only 4 wells, so weight rightly fell on the monotonic tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 and replicate high-dose texture.

Acquisition order helped: starting at maximal dose then mid-dose then a near-max replicate and a low dose established dose-dependence, while describe_phenotype provided visual bundling that quantitative tubulin increases alone could not fully discriminate.

What was right:
- High-dose tubulin intensity and texture increases (tub_glcm_contrast z>117, tub_std z>69, tub_mean z up to +58.7) correctly favored stabilization over depolymerization
- Microscopist bundling observation correctly pointed to microtubule stabilizers
- Reference atlas 5/10 stabilizer matches correctly anchored the 0.84 to 0.93 hypothesis updates
- Monotonic tub_glcm_contrast dose-response rho=+1.00 correctly confirmed dose-dependent bundling

What was wrong or missed:
- Retained Protein degradation at 0.05 based on 2/10 atlas hits despite no tubulin-bundling biology to support it
- Over-interpreted tub_mean rho=+0.80 and cell_count rho=-0.80 trends despite p=0.2 from only 4 wells; texture was the only statistically strong trend
- Under-discussed residual low-dose signal at 0.01 uM (tub_glcm_contrast z=+5.5, tub_std z=+5.2) suggesting high potency and incomplete washout to DMSO baseline

Proposed next experiment: Cell-free tubulin polymerization assay with GTP/paclitaxel controls plus immunofluorescence for bundled microtubules and phospho-histone H3 mitotic index across 0.001-3 uM to confirm direct stabilization and mitotic arrest.
